subject: Request: AWS Private Offer — revenue-split cap exemption for Orion AI
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Lang <mike.lang@orionai.com>, Orion AI Procurement <procurement@orionai.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: AWS Private Offer — revenue-split cap exemption for Orion AI

Team — quick summary and ask: Orion (attached draft) is asking for a private offer on AWS with a non-standard rev-share cap: they want a fixed 10% rev-share cap on any committed consumption above $1.2M ARR and a 60-day net payment term. This is outside the standard marketplace guidance (we typically avoid absolute caps and prefer percentage splits + tiered thresholds).

Why this is urgent: they’re ready to sign if we can accept the cap and the 60-day term; they’re a strategic prospect in our GenAI vertical and plan to migrate a large portion of their inference spend over the next 12 months. Legal flagged the cap as a precedent risk; Revenue Ops flagged margin impact (see attachment).

Ask: can we get executive approval to permit a one-off rev-share cap to accelerate close, with the following constraints: 1) cap only applies to AWS private listing and for this contract term (12 months), 2) we attach a clause that allows Redwood to revert to standard rev-share on renewal, and 3) procurement retains net60 but finance to approve a small early-pay discount if necessary.

Attaching: orion_priv_offer_draft.pdf, margin_analysis.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik: quick finance/margin sign-off and suggested guardrails
- Marissa: recommendation on commission carve-out
- Jonas: final escalation for sign-off if we can’t reconcile margins

Thanks —
Ava
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Cloud Marketplace
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: AWS Private Offer — revenue-split cap exemption for Orion AI

Ava — thanks for the context and the files. Quick read: margin_analysis shows ~8% reduction in expected unit economics if we accept a 10% absolute cap across the band they described. Two immediate considerations from Finance:
1) If we accept a 10% cap, we need either an upfront commitment or an early-pay incentive to recover unit economics (they asked for net60, so an early-pay 1.5% discount for net30 could be used).
2) We should limit the cap to spend above a threshold (e.g., only applies to consumption over $1.2M ARR) and include an explicit sunset clause tied to renewal (12 months).

I can approve a one-off cap under conditions: documented guardrails in the MSA, treasury-approved early-pay option, and Revenue Ops to confirm commission carve-out for the seller. If Marissa signs off on commission treatment, recommend we escalate to Jonas for exec approval with those constraints.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Lang <mike.lang@orionai.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: AWS Private Offer — revenue-split cap exemption for Orion AI

Team — reviewed. Commission impact: if we treat this as a one-off marketplace exception, we should carve the opportunity out of standard ACV-based comp and pay a modified accelerator tied to realized cash (to avoid overpay on inflated ARR that we may never collect). Proposed approach: pay AE a 5% override on collected revenue for the first 12 months, no accelerator thereafter. This mitigates risk for Redwood and keeps the AE team motivated.

Legal note (from my last sync with Legal): add explicit language that the rev-share cap applies only to the AWS private offer and cannot be used to set precedent across other marketplace listings or cloud regions. Also require an audit clause for reported consumption for 18 months.

If Finance (Karthik) is okay with the early-pay 1.5% discount incentive and Jonas signs off on the precedent language, I’m comfortable with the carve-out.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Lang <mike.lang@orionai.com>, Orion AI Procurement <procurement@orionai.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: AWS Private Offer — revenue-split cap exemption for Orion AI

Thanks for driving this, team. I’ve reviewed Karthik and Marissa’s recommendations. Executive decision: approved with conditions.

Conditions to be reflected in the private offer and MSA:
- Rev-share cap: 10% cap applies only to incremental consumption above $1.2M ARR for the 12-month term attached to this PO.
- Precedent clause: explicit non-precedent language — cap limited to AWS private listing for Orion AI; Redwood reserves the right to re-evaluate marketplace terms on renewal.
- Payment/treasury: Orion must accept either net30 with 1.5% early-pay discount (preferred) or net60 with a 2.5% non-recoverable surcharge to Redwood (use only if procurement insists on net60). Finance to choose which path and document in SOW.
- Audit & reporting: 18-month audit right on consumption reporting; settlement clause for reconciliations no later than 90 days after term end.
- Commission: AE compensation per Marissa’s proposal (5% on collected revenue first 12 months).

Ava — please coordinate Legal to insert these clauses and send a redlined private offer to Mike and Procurement. Once DocuSign is provisionally updated, loop me for final sign-off. I want this closed this week if possible.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Cloud Partnerships & Marketplace
Redwood Inference
